method: Read the doc in full (1193 lines), then every cited seam in the LIVE tree. Every citation below was opened and read; line numbers are live as of HEAD 171d695. Goldens recomputed by hand: T1, T2, T5, T6, T8, T12, T13.
summary: The core architecture is sound and most citations hold: composite-on-read, the premultiplied flag plus bottom-copy seed (the 50-vs-100 arithmetic is right, and bottom-copy is verbatim-exact on the CPU oracle), the (owner, tile, channel) key, and the paths-under-paint/ layout. Three findings block landing. B1: the clean-plane save skip re-stages 'existing sidecar bytes' from the TARGET directory, and every save goes through a file dialog, so saving into a new directory silently drops every clean plane. B2: dormancy is staged in 5, but stage 4 already moves fills onto their own planes, and FillLayerStates::ensure dirties every fresh state, so every v1 project with a Fill opened by a stage-4 build double-counts the fill. B3: the doc redefines read_tile/read_channel_tile as 'cache if materialized' and claims every reader is untouched, but the save loop reads Base through exactly those accessors. Once stage 4 materializes caches, a save bakes the composite into Base and every reopen double-counts every layer. Twelve MAJORs follow. The premultiplied invariant is broken by the default alpha-only eraser. The version-bump mechanism contradicts ProjectModel::new. Base becomes unreachable for the eraser, smudge and clone. The memory table under-counts by 1.2-1.9x and the advisory budget ends in a wgpu OOM panic, not a refusal. The tombstone cap is smaller than one ordinary delete. Layer-mask strokes are a composite writer the dirt model misses. The per-frame flush runs before the fill and material producers. Metadata-drag recomposite cost is unbudgeted. The mesh-map import producer is missed. Cross-document plane bleed. Dormancy misfires on v2 projects. Mid-stroke stage-3 refusals have no recovery path. Every finding carries a binding fix; folding them in is an r2 rewrite of §2.3, §4.1-4.2, §5.4, §6.2-6.3, §7 and §8, not a redesign.

blockers.failure: Paint L1 and L2, save to A (all planes written, flags cleared). Paint L1 only, then save to B. L2's planes and Base are clean, so their readback is skipped, and B has no sidecar to re-stage from, so nothing is staged. The manifest omits them, and B opens with L2 and Base empty. The loss is silent: the warning path is only logged on readback FAILURE, not on a clean skip. The failure is already live at stage 2, for Base alone: open, save, then save to a new dir loses all Base paint.

On reopen, Base = old composite, and the layers composite over it again. Every save/reopen cycle adds one more copy of every layer, silently.

majors.surface: §4.3 item 1 'Every v2 plane is premultiplied, and every writer converts' vs §3 Eraser
evidence: crates/umber-brush/src/retouch.rs:75-82,98-108: EraseParams defaults to alpha-only ('color data is left in place (unassociated)').
crates/umber-brush/src/retouch.rs:530-540: an enabled channel is scaled by k = 1 - cov, and disabled channels are byte-identical. So the alpha-only erase scales a, not rgb.
crates/umber-core/src/layers.rs:343: blend_channel clamps src to 0..1, so an un-premultiplied s = p/a > 1 clamps.
majors.failure: Opaque premultiplied red (200,0,0,255) under a 50% alpha-only erase becomes (200,0,0,128), which is invalid premultiplied data (p > a). The composite over opaque white: s_r = 200/128 = 1.5625, clamped to 1.0, cov = 0.501961, out_r = 1 + (1-1)·cov = 1.0, giving 255. The correct premultiplied erase (100,0,0,128) gives out_r = 1 + (0.78125-1)·0.501961 = 0.890196, giving 227. So every soft eraser edge renders 28 LSB too bright in red. §3 calls the eraser 'literally true' to row 19 without noting the conflict. Smudge (per-channel lerp, retouch.rs:408-411) and clone (copy) preserve p ≤ a; only the eraser breaks it.

Sampling the composite costs one additional readback of the cache, not a new class of cost.
majors.failure: Every migrated v1 project holds ALL its paint in Base (§6.3). The moment the stack has any layer, which is every real project, the eraser, smudge and clone can never touch that paint again: they act on the selected layer's (empty) plane. The same applies to a fresh session that paints with an empty stack and then adds a layer. Clone and smudge on a newly added layer, the standard clone-to-new-layer workflow, sample an EMPTY plane and do nothing. Today they sample the visible canvas. That is a user-visible regression of three P0 tools that the doc defers as a 'follow-up'.

docs/specs/requirements.md:166: the reference GPU class is 'RTX 3060 / RX 6600' (the RX 6600 is 8 GB).
majors.recomputed_table: 4K, 5 Base channels, as the doc assumes. Row 2 (6 paint layers × 2 ch): planes 768 + Base 320 + cache 2×64 = 1,216 MiB (doc: 1,088). Row 3 (+2 materials × 4 ch): planes 1,280 + Base 320 + cache ≤5×64 = 1,920 MiB (doc: 1,600). Row 4 (×4 UDIM): 5,120 + 1,280 + 1,280 = 7,680 MiB (doc: 6,400). Add +16 MiB per quick-mask-gated plane.
majors.failure: The honest row-4 figure (7.5 GiB) exceeds the 8 GB reference card once the framebuffer, mesh and env maps are counted. The 'advisory, never enforced' judgment (:230-236) rests on 'refusing is a silent data-path failure the never-crash doctrine forbids'. The actual alternative it picks is an allocation failure the app has no handler for: a crash, the outcome the doctrine forbids most.

evidence: per-layer-pool-design.md:747-749: the doc's own example, 'Deleting one 4-channel material across 4 tiles retires 16 planes = 1 GiB at 4K', is TWICE the 512 MiB cap. A single-tile 4-channel material is 256 MiB, so two deletes fill the cap.

per-layer-pool-design.md:735-739: retirement is a 'read back to CPU' in the per-frame census. That is 16 blocking 64 MiB readbacks (PaintTarget::read_back_rgba8, as in paint_state.rs:2654) in ONE frame.
Fills and materials are EVAL-owned (§5.1:631-635, §5.2) and re-evaluable from layer params, which the revived layer carries (journal.rs:59-66, Insert holds the full Layer).
majors.failure: (a) The doc doesn't specify what happens when one tombstone alone exceeds the cap. 'Free the OLDEST first' then frees the tombstone just created, so the delete is immediately un-undoable, with a status line, on every ordinary material delete at 4 tiles. (b) A multi-hundred-ms to multi-second hitch on delete. (c) 'Resize drops contents' (§5.5) says nothing about tombstones, so a revive after a resize uploads old-size bytes that publish rejects, and the layer revives empty. (d) 1 GiB of RAM is spent preserving pixels that one re-eval regenerates.

A metadata snapshot cannot see a pixel edit inside a mask plane.
§4.4:606-613: under CoR, layer masks 'finally gate something live', for every channel of the layer.
majors.failure: A literal implementation either never recomposites a mask stroke, so the mask paints invisibly until some unrelated edit raises Full, or diffs whole mask planes per frame / raises Full on every mask frame. That is a 16.8M-texel recomposite per channel per frame, plus full-plane mask uploads, for the duration of every mask stroke. A material layer's mask edit dirties ALL its declared channels, not stroke_channel.

majors.surface: §4.1 judgment part 1 (flush placement) + §5.3 anchor partial flatten
evidence: crates/umber-app/src/main.rs:2894-2899 is the drain. The fill refresh (:2906-2955) and material refresh (:2958-3041) run AFTER it in the same update and publish WriteRegion into thread queues that are only executed by the NEXT process_pending.

per-layer-pool-design.md:485-493: the flush 'runs right after the existing per-frame drain … GPU binders … see the end-of-frame flush'. It does not run at the end of the frame, and the plane commands queued after it are not yet on the GPU.
crates/umber-gpu/src/paint_thread.rs:150-160: each plane has its own mpsc command queue. The composite reads plane TEXTURES, so queued-but-unprocessed commands are invisible to it.
majors.failure: (a) A fill/material refresh displays one frame late. (b) Worse, an anchored material whose anchor prefix contains a fill refreshed THIS frame: §5.3's GPU partial flatten composites the prefix planes while the fill's WriteRegion still sits in that plane's mpsc queue. The anchor reads the stale fill, the material evaluates on stale input, and nothing re-dirties it. The anchor read is silently one edit stale, with no next-frame self-heal, because the material is now clean.

evidence: per-layer-pool-design.md:462,514-518: any opacity/blend/visibility/reorder/mask-enable/material-channel-param change marks Full for every (tile, channel) the layer has a plane on, recomposited on the per-frame flush.

egui sliders emit a change every frame while dragged, so a material layer at 5 channels × 4 tiles raises 20 Full recomposites per frame, each L_c × 16.8M texel-ops. Every masked entry in each re-uploads its whole 16 MiB mask (compositor.rs:1029-1036) and, for overridden channels, CPU-resamples the set-size mask (§4.4:611-613, resample_mask_nearest).

per-layer-pool-design.md:467-472 sizes the per-frame rect for strokes only ('a 4-dab event union ≈ 7,500 texels'). DirtyRegion is ONE union rect (:512-513), and symmetry siblings and seam mirrors (paint_state.rs:2287-2305, 2402-2405) land on the far side of the tile in the same event. A mirrored dab pair at x≈100 and x≈3996 unions to a near-full-width rect, and diagonal seam mirrors to the full tile.
majors.failure: Neither the opacity-drag nor the symmetry/seam path is costed, and both plausibly blow the 16.7 ms frame and the 20 ms input-to-photon budgets the doc claims the region path protects. The stage-4 perf gate re-measures input-to-photon only for plain strokes.

The user's next baseColor stroke lands in the AO import layer's plane. The imported map itself renders nothing under CoR (the layer has no plane), although per-layer storage is exactly what would let it render.

verified_holds: F3/§4.3 arithmetic: the dab splat is premultiplied over (shaders.rs:584-587: src = dab.color*coverage; out = src + dst*(1-src.a)), and Dab.color is premultiplied (paint.rs:43). composite_pixel_masked is the straight-alpha lerp with Porter-Duff alpha (compositor.rs:693-729). Over a transparent accumulator, P=100, A=128 treated as straight: 0.392157·0.501961 = 0.196847, ×255 = 50.196, giving 50; with un-premultiply, s = 0.78125 and out = 0.392157 → 100. Both correct and ≥0.1 from the rounding boundaries.

Un-premultiply then lerp equals premultiplied over for Normal at any accumulator, in exact arithmetic: base + (p/a − base)·a = p + base·(1−a). Bottom-copy on CPU is exact: acc = b/255, f32_to_u8 (compositor.rs:644-653) returns b. Empty stack: output clears (judgment 7). Masked first entry: bottom-copy correctly does NOT fire (requires unmasked). A texture copy for the GPU seed is feasible: PaintTarget has COPY_SRC|COPY_DST (paint.rs:276-280).
T2: s = 200/100 = 2.0, clamped to 1.0 by blend_channel (layers.rs:343), out = 100/255, giving 100; bottom-copy keeps 200. Correct.
§6.1 prune hazard is real: prune_stale_layer_files remove_dir_all (project.rs:436-480, :467-469/:475). Keeping planes under paint/ is correct.
F2: TilePool keys a u8 ChannelKind tag (tile_pool.rs:127-145), so Data channels collide. Rejecting it as the store is correct.

§2.3: check_paintable's `_ => Ok(())` arm and NOTE are live (layers.rs:1356-1376). InstanceError derives Clone (layers.rs:76), so storing Result<(), InstanceError> on PaintState is buildable. Path replays go through begin_stroke_styled (paint_state.rs:1764-1840) and inherit the gate. The quick-mask edit hook ordering (paint_state.rs:2340-2364) matches the doc.
spp_import.rs and psd_import.rs do not write the pool (no PaintState calls). The autosave journal carries no pixel op (journal.rs:48-66; main.rs:74-80), so §6.4 holds.
unverified: U1: whether eframe/egui-wgpu 0.36 installs a device uncaptured-error handler. No handler exists in crates/ (grep). If eframe installs one that logs instead of panicking, M4's failure becomes 'silently black/garbage planes' rather than a crash.
